rationale: THE `mixes_in` RELABEL'S CONTRACT (2026-10-23, rung R3 — NO grammar change). A php trait `use` composes a trait into a type: the trait's members are flattened into the composing type, no module is imported and no binding surface is created. The ten could not spell that honestly — `uses` asserts a value READ, `imports` asserts a module binding — and the vocabulary was extended exactly for shapes of this kind (src/ast/types.ts:75-90,155-162). The fleet has already published this relabel at R3 twice with no grammar change: ruby's include/extend/prepend (real-ruby-analyzer.ts:2263-2280) and javascript's call-shaped heritage. THE RELABEL IS 1:1: source (the composing type), target (the trait's leaf), confidence (1.0), line (the trait name) and the `isTraitUse` marker all stay; only the stored TYPE changes, and the evidence tier follows the CONSTRUCT — a declaration-header grammar clause is DECLARED-STRUCTURAL, which is why these rows pin `meta.evidenceClass: "structural"` where they used to pin `usage_contextual`. The fixture pins the shape in both directions, because a relabel that can be silently reverted is not pinned: the six composition rows are REQUIRED as `mixes_in`, the old `uses` row for the same pair is FORBIDDEN, and the three impostors are pinned apart — a namespace import is `imports`, a closure capture is a `uses` read of the captured binding, and the adaptation block's `Named::label as private renamed` names a METHOD (an alias inside the composition directive), so neither `label` nor `renamed` may become a target of any composition row. Multi-trait `use Named, HasId;` is TWO rows (one per trait), trait-on-trait composition is a row, an enum composes a trait (php 8.1), and a QUALIFIED trait name publishes the LEAF target exactly as every other heritage/mixin target in this lane does. THE POPULATION THIS SHAPE HAS is measured by script/m14/php-population.ts --emit (whole-population trait-use census); this file is the CONTRACT and the census is the COUNT, and neither is a substitute for the other.

expectRelationships.comment: TRAIT COMPOSES TRAIT: `trait Composite { use Named; }`. mixes_in is not a class-only relation, and the source is the composing trait.
MULTI-TRAIT, first of two: `use Named, HasId;` is two rows, one per trait — a single row naming the list would be a target nobody can write.
ADAPTATION FORM: `use Named { Named::label as private renamed; }` composes ONE trait, Named; the alias inside the block names a METHOD and is forbidden as a target below.

QUALIFIED TRAIT NAME: `use \Lib\Remote;` publishes the LEAF target (`Remote`), which is the lane's heritage/mixin leaf rule; the trait need not be declared in this file — the directive is what the source writes.
AN ENUM COMPOSES A TRAIT (php 8.1): the composing type is the enum itself, not a case.
IMPOSTOR 1, the positive half: a NAMESPACE import of a same-named class is `imports` and stays `imports` — the relabel moves the trait-composition class, not the import class.
IMPOSTOR 2, the positive half: `function () use ($x)` CAPTURES a value — a read of the binding (php's variable-read spelling `<source>\u0000<binding>`), never a composition.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: ONE row per (composing type, trait): a doubled row would mean the adaptation/sibling walk emitted twice, which the store's relId dedup would hide from every other instrument.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE NEGATIVE HALF OF THE RELABEL: the exact row this fixture replaced. A revert to `uses` leaves the same edge in the same place with the same metadata and every consumer that only counts edges passes — this forbid is what makes the relabel load-bearing.

IMPOSTOR: the method named inside an adaptation block (`Named::label as ...`) is a MEMBER of the trait, not a trait. A composition row to it would be a composition of a name the directive does not compose.
IMPOSTOR: the ALIAS created by the adaptation block is a method name, not a trait — publishing it would invent a trait the source does not name.
IMPOSTOR 1's negative half: a trait composition must never be published as a module import (the ten's OTHER dishonest spelling for this construct).
